prompt:
Is everyone in crunch waiting for one slow thread? Which one, and why?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: yes

## Bottleneck and wait chain

Across the whole trace (offsets **0–30,517 ms**), **calc-3 (TID 636275)** is a significant bottleneck for crunch (PID 636270). It ended **7,684 ms across 18 waits** by waking the main thread, accounting for **77.5% of the main thread’s waits on other threads**. Crunch’s rounds averaged **426.962 ms**; calc-3 finished **416.322 ms after its calc-* peers** on average.

The chain is: **crunch waited on calc-3, which was held up waiting for CPU time**. Calc-3 averaged **416.708 ms waiting for a CPU per round**, despite running for **10.180 ms**. This was CPU contention within the process: the CPU was held by **monitor (TID 636280, real-time priority 10) for 99.8%** of calc-3’s CPU-wait time. The process was **not globally oversubscribed**: on average, 3.0 of its threads were ready to run across the 8 CPUs it used. Runnable time means a thread is ready but not running; substantial runnable time can indicate scheduling delay [3].

One typical instance was at **14,492 ms**: crunch’s wait lasted **560.096 ms**; calc-3 was preempted for **550.090 ms**, then ran for **10.006 ms** and woke crunch.

## Is it literally everyone?

Not literally: the **watchdog** was idle, and **monitor** was active. The calc-* peers generally waited for crunch to give them work; those waits are not evidence that they were themselves the bottleneck. The analysis follows the main thread’s progress through its causal wait chain to identify the hold-up [1].

The delay was **consistent across all 18 rounds**, not just occasional spikes: the median was about **560.042 ms**, with no anomalies reported. TMLL lists **466 futex calls** for calc-3 totaling **27,564.830 ms**; that total includes its waits for new work, so it is not all time holding crunch up. The main-thread wait-chain result isolates the relevant portion.

### All sources used:
1) Critical Path (Process Wait Analysis) - https://archive.eclipse.org/tracecompass/doc/stable/org.eclipse.tracecompass.doc.user/LTTng-Kernel-Analysis.html  
3) Runnable time and CPU contention - https://archive.eclipse.org/tracecompass/doc/stable/org.eclipse.tracecompass.doc.user/LTTng-Kernel-Analysis.html
